Golden beams lance through cathedral clouds, flooding the docks in honey light.
Soft pink dawn bleeds across the cloud-sea, tender and still.
The sun hangs enormous at the horizon, burning copper through the haze.
Thin mist drifts between the moored islands, soft as a held breath.
A rainbow arcs through the amber cloud-banks, vivid and trembling.
Warm lantern-glow spills across the dock planks at dusk.
The cloud-sea below glows amber, deep and slow-burning.
Cumulus towers catch the late sun, blazing white at their crowns.
A gentle sun-shower falls in silver threads through golden air.
A rainbow blooms behind the rain, quiet and enormous.
First stars appear in the deep violet above the harbor.
Twilight softens everything to lavender and fading rose.
The full moon lays a silver road across the cloud-sea.
Moonlight glazes the clouds below in cold, trembling silver.
Sky-koi drift in silhouette against the wide burning sun.
Birds wheel in black arcs across the white face of the sun.
Shafts of golden-hour light pour through a gap in the cloud-wall.
The cloud-sea ripples amber and rose in the last of the light.
A single long sunbeam reaches across the harbor, warm and slow.
Mist threads through the rigging, soft and luminous.
The horizon glows a deep molten gold beneath the giant setting sun.
Pale blue light lingers at the edges of the clouds after sunset.
Cumulus billows catch pink light from below, glowing like lanterns.
The sun-shower fades, leaving the air bright and washed clean.
Lanterns along the moorings bloom gold against the deepening dusk.
